content.text: Punjab Ayush Counselling is the admission procedure undertaken for Ayush courses: BAMS/BNYS/BUMS/BSMS/BHMS. Guru Ravidas Ayurved University, Punjab , conducts the state counselling for Ayush. Admissions are offered solely based on the NEET scores to various Ayurveda, Homeopathy, and Unani colleges in Punjab. The state counselling offers seats through the state quota and the All India Quota.

The NEET-UG 2025 examination was conducted on May 4, 2025, and the results were published on June 14, 2025. The Punjab Ayush Counselling 2025 dates are yet to be announced officially by the authorities.
Continue reading the article to learn more about the Punjab Ayush counselling details, such as eligibility, fees, cutoff, counselling process, and more.

sections.heading: Punjab Ayush Counselling Overview

content.text: Admission to BAMS, BHMS, and BUMS institutions in Punjab is accepted through the Punjab state Ayush Counselling, which is conducted by the Guru Ravidas Ayurved University, Punjab. The primary requirement for participation in the counselling is to qualify NEET-UG examination, conducted by the NTA. The qualified candidates further need to register for the counselling on the Punjab Ayush Counselling official website of https://grauadmission.smartpad.in/.

In Punjab, the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine(NCISM) and National Commission for Homeopathy(NCH) regulate the private and government Ayush Colleges. There are a total of 19 BAMS colleges , 4 BHMS colleges, and 1 BUMS college in the state.

The 85% seats in the state are reserved for the students who are residents of Punjab under the State Quota, and the remaining 15% seats are under the All India Quota (AIQ), through which students from other states can also apply to the Ayush colleges in Punjab. The AACCC is in charge of conducting the All India Quota (AIQ) counselling.

sections.heading: Punjab Ayush Counselling Process

content.text: Punjab Ayush Counselling for admission to Ayush private and government colleges in the state is offered through two different quotas, the State quota and the All India Quota.

items: The State Quota reserves 15% of the seats for its domicile students.

All India Quota (AIQ) is open to all categories of students, including students from other states/ non-domicile students. The counselling is handled by the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee, AACCC .

sections.heading: Punjab Ayush Counselling Process for State Quota

content.text: The procedures involved in the Punjab state Ayush counselling under the state quota are mentioned below.

Registration: The candidates must register with the Punjab Ayush Counselling official website of https://grauadmission.smartpad.in/ and submit the application form. Fill out the application form with the necessary details and upload your signature and photo. Make payment of the fee to register successfully.
Merit List: The Merit list is published on the official website according to the candidates’ NEET ranks.
Choice Filling: Based on the Merit List, the candidates must fill in their preference for colleges and lock their choices.

Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on the NEET scores and other factors such as the reservation policy, the seat matrix of colleges, and the choice of colleges. Upon the publication of Allotment results, candidates must log in to the official portal and download the Punjab Ayush Counselling Allotment Letter.

Document Verification and Joining the College: Candidates must report to the allotted college with the original documents and certificates to get them verified and complete the admission procedure, including college fee payment.

Note: The counselling is held in 4 rounds: Round 1/Round 2/ Round 3/ Stray Vacancy Round. Fresh applications are accepted till the 3rd Round. The candidates who were not allotted seats, did not join the allotted college, or gave willingness to upgrade seats can participate in the subsequent rounds without registering again. Stray vacancy round allotment is made only for the vacant seats after the previous rounds.

sections.heading: Punjab Ayush Counselling Process for All India Quota (AIQ)

content.text: The procedures involved in the Punjab Ayush counselling under the All India Quota are mentioned below.

Registration & Fee Payment: Register with the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in by providing the necessary personal and academic details and uploading the relevant certificates and documents. Make payment of the counselling fees to submit the application successfully.
Choice Filling/ Locking: candidates need to choose the state and colleges according to their preference. It is mandatory to lock the choices before the last date.
Allotment of Seats: Allotment is made based on the NEET-UG score, reservation policy, seat availability, and choice of colleges by the candidates.
Publishing of Allotment Result: Log in to the portal and download the Provisional Allotment Order.

Physical Reporting to College: The candidates must report to the college allotted with the original certificates and documents for verification, and complete the admission formalities by making the college fee payment.
Learn more about the counselling process under the All India Quota, read the article on Ayush NEET Counselling 2025 .

The Punjab Ayush counselling is conducted by the Guru Ravidas Ayurved University under both the State Quota and All India Quota. cells: The candidates must have 10+2 from a recognized university and 12th grade in the science with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (PCB subjects).
A minimum aggregate of 50% must be obtained in the PCB subjects by the general category candidates, and an aggregate of 40% by the SC/ST/OBC candidates.
NEET-UG 2025 is compulsory for participation in the counselling.
The age of the applicants must be at least 17 years in the year of admission.
The candidate’s eligibility and merit will be determined by the Selection Committee as per the rules of Punjab Govt. Notifications.
